Criterion B3 (avoidance of reminders): MET — patient avoids places and conversations that trigger memories. Criterion B4 (inability to recall details): MET — patient reported difficulty recalling important parts of the trauma. Criterion C1 (negative beliefs): MET — patient experiences negative feelings about self and the world. Criterion C2 (self-blame): UNCLEAR — patient indicated excessive self-blame but not consistently. Criterion C3 (negative emotional state): MET — patient reported feelings of fear, anger, and guilt. Criterion C4 (diminished interest): MET — patient noted a significant decrease in interest in activities. Criterion C5 (detachment): MET — patient described feeling distant from others. Criterion C6 (inability to experience positive emotions): MET — patient reported difficulty feeling positive emotions. Criterion D1 (irritability): MET — patient described increased irritability and outbursts. Criterion D2 (recklessness): MET — patient mentioned engaging in self-destructive behaviors. Criterion D3 (hypervigilance): MET — patient reported feeling more on guard. Criterion D4 (startle response): MET — patient noted being more easily startled. Criterion D5 (concentration difficulties): MET — patient described difficulty concentrating. Criterion D6 (sleep disturbances): MET — patient reported disrupted sleep. Criterion E (duration): MET — symptoms began after the traumatic event and have persisted for more than one month. Criterion F (functional impairment): MET — patient indicated significant distress and interference with daily functioning. Criterion G (exclusion): MET — patient denied substance use or medical conditions affecting symptoms. Total: 14 of 20 criteria met (threshold ≥ 1). Diagnosis: TRUE — full criteria for PTSD met with significant functional impairment confirmed.
